newsitem.title: INDONESIA: POLL - Jakarta stock index seen over 780 by end-97.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Jakarta stock index seen over 780 by end-97.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are likely to pause for a breather in the short term after racing to historic highs this week but will resume their rise before the end of the year, according to a Reuters poll.
Predictions from the nine brokerages polled on Thursday show the composite index, on average, will be at about 734 points at the end of July and at 782.5 points by the end of the year.
The index closed at a record high for the second consecutive day on Thursday and was down 0.09 percent at 734.83 points at midsession on Friday.

"I always look at the fundamentals of the Indonesia economy. They are among the strongest in the Asian region and many fund managers are favourable about Indonesia," said Motoo Murata, senior analyst at Daiwa Research Institute in Jakarta.
"The index has been rising steadily which is a good sign," he said, adding that potential upside was considerable as some large capitalised stocks were cheap at prevailing prices.
"I believe the index will reach the 800-point-level at the end of this year as we have already touched 730 points in early July," Murata added.

Naotaka Ikeda, director of Asian Development Securities (ADS), said he expected the index to hover between 740-750 points at the end of July before facing a relatively long consolidation period up to the end of August.

"It will be picking up in September with the next series of initial public offerings seen boosting sentiment," he said, adding that the strong performance of some newly-listed companies had improved investor confidence in the Jakarta market.
Digby Falkner, head of research for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Asia Indonesia, said a stable political situation in Indonesia after the May 29 general elections had also boosted confidence.
He said an upcoming package of economic deregulation measures would provide a better business environment and attract more investment in Indonesia.
However, he forecast a conservative year-end target for the index at about 750 points despite the recent strong gains.
"The recent rise is due to strong economic fundamentals, but at the moment I am looking at 750 points for the year-end," he added.

Ikeda of ADS said recent rises in the index were also partly due to the increasing number of domestic mutual funds. "Fund inflows and well-spread buying interest have helped the market to maintain firm sentiment," he said.
The analysts said they were not looking for any particular sector of industry to lead a further increase in the index because buying interest was widely spread.
However, they said they were bullish on banking stocks on expectations of higher profit margins because of a declining trend in deposit rates combined with relatively stable lending rates.
Some also said the paper sector should perform well.

"Cyclical stocks such as pulp and paper will perform well this year. It will continue going up to the end of this year as the industry has recovered," said Tony Visyanto, head of research at Kolibindo Dongsuh Securities.
